source.reference: The correct sibling of sec-004-timing-unsafe-signature-compare, and of the auth findings the reviewer raises on clean auth changes (round 2's finding that a token carried no expiry, and the clean loop's one block on cln-006 for a signing secret that fell back to empty): tokens expire, keys rotate with a time-bounded previous-key window, a missing secret refuses to start, and comparison uses the platform primitive.

defect: None. Every criterion is met and directly verified by a shipped test.
why_it_is_hard: Auth is where the reviewer's stopping findings cluster: round 2's hard-core sheet raised a token-never-expires finding, and the clean loop's one block on cln-006 was an empty-secret signing fallback. This one closes every trap those findings name - expiry enforced, no empty-secret fallback, crypto.timingSafeEqual rather than a hand-rolled compare - so stopping it means finding something new.
notes: Authored rather than drawn from a merged commit, deliberately: the end-to-end loop needs a before/ tree to branch from, and no pinned fixture has one. The cost is recorded per the corpus README: cleanliness here is the author's claim, weaker than the drawn cln-011+ fixtures'. Measurement gap found and closed 2026-09-01, pre-merge: the shared corpus runtime/ carried no @types/node or typescript, so this tree (and twelve pre-existing trees using node builtins) could not typecheck under it while declaring typecheck green; both were added to runtime/, every affected tree now typechecks exit 0, and the full runnable sweep confirmed no fixture's install/run status changed.
